name: CodeBlock
summary: Read-only code display, with line numbers and syntax colors when you pass the highlighter.

a11y.apg: No APG pattern: it is <pre><code>, and native semantics are what a screen reader needs — the <pre> preserves the line structure that the code depends on. Without `copyable` there is nothing to focus. With it, the copy button is a real <button> with an accessible name, reachable by Tab like any other. With `lineNumbers`, the numbers are CSS generated content with an empty alternative text: screen readers skip them, and selecting or copying the code brings only the code.

props.name: children
props.description: The code, as a string and not as nodes: it goes verbatim inside <code>, so whitespace and line breaks are yours to control.

props.name: language
props.description: Written to data-language, which labels the block, and handed to `highlight`, which picks the grammar by it: tsx, ts, jsx, js, css, html, json and bash.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Draws the copy button. The copying itself lives in the core's aurea.js, so React and plain HTML share one implementation instead of two that drift.

props.name: preview
props.description: The live example of the code. With it, the block becomes the example box of Aurea's site: the Preview | Code tabs (a segmented control across the width; arrows, Home and End move between them), the preview on the recessed surface and the code without a frame.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Shows the number of each line on the left, in a 16px column 24px from the code. The column grows with the digits of the last line, so it does not jump at line 100. The number is drawing: it is not in the copied text and not read by screen readers.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Colors the code. Pass `highlightCode` from `@aurea-uds/react/code-highlight`; its grammars are optional peers (@lezer/javascript, @lezer/css, @lezer/html, @lezer/json, @codemirror/legacy-modes). A language it does not know comes back plain. The colors are the same as the CodeEditor's, mixed 20% with the text so each one reads at 4.5:1 or more on the block.

props.name: className
props.description: Lands on the outer element either way — on the <pre> when plain, on the wrapper when copyable.
